pathways.label: Investor visa (VITEM IX)

pathways.label: Retirement / passive-income residency
pathways.notes: Permanent residence for retirees or persons with stable monthly transfer income (pension, dividends, rentals) transferred from abroad — proof of ~$2,000+/month and health coverage typical. Lower capital than investor route; popular in Florianópolis and coastal cities.

pathways.label: Digital nomad visa (VITEM XIV)

Alternative: ~$18,000 lump sum / R$100,000 bank balance accepted in place of monthly income (2026 consular guidance).

critical_tests.notes: Mercosur mobility after naturalization (~10 countries). Active Bitcoin/Lightning fintech scene in São Paulo. Crypto taxed as assets (15–22.5% on gains above thresholds) — plan treasury structure before relocating.

legal_compliance.property_foreign_ownership: Foreigners may purchase urban real estate freely; rural land near borders restricted. Coastal properties follow standard civil registry rules — fideicomiso not required.

pathways.label: Temporary resident (economic solvency)
pathways.notes: 2026 economic solvency (July 2025 consular guidelines; UMA 2026 = 117.31 MXN): EITHER ~US$4,400/month net income over the last 6–12 months OR ~US$74,000 in savings/investments maintained for 12 months (consulates vary ±5–10%; e.g. Tucson $73,215, Las Vegas $78,025). 1–4 year renewable. Crypto and precious metals are NOT accepted as proof. Sources: Mexperience 2026 criteria (fetched 2026-09-10); MexLaw UMA calc (2026-01-28); consulate pages (2025-12/2026).

pathways.label: Investor visa (capital investment)
pathways.notes: Capital investment route: MXN 5,378,664 (≈US$300,000 at 18 MXN/USD, 2026) into a Mexican company or listed securities — qualifies for temporary residency (permanent via 4-year upgrade or direct solvency). Property-ownership route also exists: residential property valued ≥MXN 10,758,500 (≈US$598,000), lien-free, in Mexico. Source: Mexperience 2026 investment criteria (fetched 2026-09-10).

pathways.label: Permanent resident (after 4 years temporary)
pathways.notes: Upgrade from temporary status after 4 consecutive years — no new capital required if compliance maintained.

critical_tests.notes: Territorial tax for non-Mexico income in practice for many structures; active Bitcoin community in CDMX, Tulum, Puerto Vallarta. Citizenship after 5 years.

Crypto/precious metals explicitly excluded from solvency proof. Bitcoin legal since 2017; FinTech Law virtual-asset regime unchanged; INM fees up for 2026 (PR card MXN 13,578.96).

programs.bitcoin_integration: Small island nation in the Gulf of Guinea offering a citizenship-by-investment program via contribution fund. Relevant to MotoPass as an affordable, fast, fully-remote CBI option rather than a Bitcoin-native one.

programs.details: São Tomé and Príncipe operates a Citizenship by Investment programme via a contribution to the national development fund: minimum ~USD 90,000–95,000 single applicant, fully remote with NO residence, physical-presence, travel or language requirement. Processing advertised at around six weeks. Applicants must be 18+, in good health, with clean criminal record and a provable source of funds; a USD ~5,000 submission fee applies (USD ~5,000 per additional dependent). Program is newer and smaller than the Caribbean CBI bloc; rules should be verified against official/embassy channels before structuring. MotoPass entry is honest and tagged Researching — not yet Satohash-stamped.
